label: first copy-phase step (input = original token 0, outputting token 1)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at step t = L+1, the step right after <DEL>, where the model reads back original token 0 as input and outputs original token 1 (~91% of such steps are active; 99% of activation mass). Never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter step. A weak residual tail appears at recall_idx 2 (1% of mass), mostly when the token 1 is digit 1. Magnitude is largest for short sequences (L=3-4) and is strongly boosted when the first original token is the digit 1 (top examples are all 1 followed by h/r/y); typical long-sequence (L=8-9) activations are small and account for most false positives (inactive cases).

issues: Every claim I tested holds. The feature never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter step (0 active steps for either). At recall_idx 1 the active rate is 0.913 and those steps hold 0.989 of the activation mass. recall_idx 2 has a rate of 0.025 and 0.011 of the mass, and recall_idx 3 or later has only 3 active steps.

The recall_idx 2 tail is a real pattern, not random noise. It is mostly copy-phase step 2 where the input is the digit '1' (orig(1) == '1'). The predicate (recall_idx==2)&(orig(1)==tok('1')) has precision 0.72 on test. The explanation already mentions this tail, and it holds only about 1% of the mass, so it does not overturn the label.

Adding the tail gives a small gain. (recall_idx == 1) | ((recall_idx==2) & (orig(1)==tok('1'))) scores test F1 0.950 and mass recall 0.9999, compared with F1 0.942 and mass recall 0.989 for the original predicate.

The length claim checks out. With L>=8, recall_idx==1 has precision 0.82 (overall 0.91). Those steps account for about 30.5k of the 43.7k false positives (about 70%), and their mass share is low relative to their step count.
The digit-1 claim checks out. (recall_idx==1)&(orig(0)==tok('1')) has precision 1.0. It covers 3.6% of active steps but 9.9% of the mass, and 14% of the top activation quartile.
